plan_a_advantages: Reduced risk of overtraining due to the high volume of easy runs.
Potentially better for an athlete who is new to structured training or recovering from an injury.
plan_b_advantages: Directly addresses key trail running demands (climbing, power) with hill and threshold work.
Includes a longer run, which is important for building endurance and simulating race conditions.
reasoning: Plan B is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It incorporates more targeted training stimuli, specifically hill work and threshold runs, which are crucial for developing the power and strength needed for trail running. Plan A, conversely, focuses almost entirely on easy runs, which while beneficial for recovery, won't significantly improve speed or climbing ability. Plan B’s inclusion of a dedicated hill session and threshold work directly addresses the demands of trail running, while Plan A’s repetitive easy runs risk leading to plateaus.  Furthermore, the inclusion of a longer run in Plan B is more aligned with the needs of a trail runner seeking to increase endurance.
